title: Diff-aware regression throttle and semantic SLA reporter
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a CI hook that throttles regression enforcement based on semantic distribution diffs and a reporter that maps eval signals to per-cohort semantic SLAs. Backwards-compatible migration and gradual rollout; no user-facing API changes.
body:
Motivation: Large regressions in eval metrics are frequently localized to a subset of prompts (e.g., a single new prompt seed or a topical cohort). Today our gates are binary and can cause noisy global rollbacks. This PR implements a diff-aware throttle that computes semantic-weighted distribution shifts and enforces a progressive quarantine/throttle policy. It also adds a semantic-SLA reporter that translates evaluation metrics into per-cohort SLOs (error-rate, latency-percentile and semantic-degradation) so on-call and product teams can reason about impact at the right granularity.

What this PR does (summary):
- New CI hook: hooks/ci/diff_aware_throttle.py — computes a semantically-weighted KS-style delta across prompt cohorts and outputs a throttle score used by the CI decision buffer.
- New reporter: reporters/semantic_sla/reporter.py — converts eval outputs into time-series SLOs and an approximation of how far an observed run is from SLA thresholds; publishes a compact JSON artifact used by the console.
- Metrics and traces: metrics/sem_sla_metrics.md + tracing hooks so each throttle decision and SLA delta is captured for post-mortem.
- Tests: unit tests for the weighting and throttle heuristic, an integration-style smoke harness that runs a small model against seeded prompt cohorts.
- Docs: docs/ci/diff-throttle.md with configuration knobs and rollout guidance.

Design notes:
- Semantically-weighted delta: prompts are embedded via the eval-harness embedding pipeline; cohort-level histograms are compared using a weighted Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) that prioritizes semantic mass rather than raw counts. This reduces noisy enforcement when the absolute count is small but semantics matter.
- Progressive quarantine: the throttle outputs a score in [0,1] which the CI decision buffer maps to actions: 0 -> allow merge, 0.1-0.4 -> gated canary (require canary run), 0.4-0.8 -> partial quarantine (block merge for flagged cohorts, allow non-impacted cohorts), 0.8+ -> full block. The mapping is configurable via ci/config.toml.
- Semantic SLA reporter: a small rule engine maps metric deltas to SLA signals (example: if semantic-degradation>0.05 for a cohort and latency-95 increases by 20ms, mark SLA as degraded). The reporter emits both human-readable summaries and structured JSON for the console ingestion pipeline.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Backwards compatible: if embeddings are not available the throttle falls back to a count-based delta (current behavior); the reporter will emit warnings but not fail.
- Gradual enablement: default off. Ship as an opt-in CI hook and a console ingestion endpoint. Suggested rollout: enable on non-blocking tier for two weeks, then move to gated canary, then to quarantine mapping.

Testing and validation: included unit tests (tests/unit/test_throttle.py), integration smoke (tests/integration/smoke_sem_sla.py) and a synthetic replay harness (tools/replay/synthetic_cohort_replay.py) to reproduce regression patterns. Run locally via `tox -e smoke` and CI runs evaluate against a tiny model to validate semantics and performance.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc and sync with SRE and console teams
- [x] Implementation of throttle algorithm + reporter
- [x] Unit tests and smoke integration tests
- [x] Docs and rollout guidance
- [x] Metrics/tracing hooks added

Notes for reviewers: pay particular attention to the weighting heuristic in diff_aware_throttle.py (function: compute_semantic_delta) and edge-case handling when cohorts are sparse. I wired a debug flag to store intermediate embeddings for one-off investigation.

Observability: new metrics emitted: eval.throttle.score, eval.throttle.action, eval.semantic_sla.delta_{cohort}, eval.semantic_sla.slo_status. Traces include the throttle decision tree and top-K prompts that contributed to the score.

Security: no secrets or credentials are introduced. The reporter output is sanitized to avoid exposing raw prompts; it only publishes cohort ids and anonymized exemplar hashes when configured.

Follow-ups:
- Hook into console UX for cohort-level visualization (ENG-4891)
- Auto-suggest rollback patches for quarantined cohorts based on exemplar diffs

Summary: This PR reduces noisy, global regression rollbacks by making the CI gate semantics-aware and provides an SLA-oriented reporting artifact to make regression impact tangible to downstream teams.

review_comments: Jonah Blake: Nice approach. Two asks: 1) can you add a small sensitivity test for embedding noise? 2) make the mapping table for throttle->action also configurable via feature flags?

Author (Aisha Kapoor): Thanks Jonah — added sensitivity unit (tests/unit/test_throttle.py::test_embedding_noise_sensitivity) and moved the mapping into ci/config.toml with defaults. See commit d4f5a6b.
Rui Chen: I worry about EMD cost at scale. Can we cap to sampled exemplars and fall back to approximate hashing?

Author (Aisha Kapoor): Good point — throttle runs in CI context and uses a sampling window; compute_semantic_delta has a sample_size param and a fast LSH-based estimate path (configurable). Added microbenchmarks under tools/replay/bench_emds.md.
Lina Morales: approve after minor doc clarifications and making sure the reporter doesn't include raw prompt text in artifacts.
Author (Aisha Kapoor): Removed raw prompts from artifacts and added exemplar hashing; updated docs accordingly.
ci_checks: integration-eval: flaky on first run -> rerun -> pass
summary: Implements a semantic-aware CI gate that throttles enforcement by distributional impact and a reporter that converts eval outputs into per-cohort SLA signals; includes tests, docs, and rollout guidance
